prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean (A) a general plain‑English beginner course that uses real numbers in examples, or (B) an educator that runs real money and publishes a full track record including losing trades? Those are different things — the former is easy to find, the latter is rare.

If you want a single recommended “stack” that meets your criteria (plain language + real numbers + transparency about losses), use this combo:

- Coin Bureau — best plain‑English, beginner‑friendly guides and explainer videos. Clear, non‑technical, good step‑by‑step walkthroughs of wallets, exchanges, tokens, and risks. (Doesn’t run a fund, so no P&L ledger.)
- Glassnode / CoinMetrics — on‑chain analytics that “show real numbers”: supply stats, flows, realized cap, exchange balances, on-chain transactions. Use these to verify claims you read elsewhere.
- Rekt (and Rekt.news) + DeFiLlama exploits pages — very transparent reporting of hacks, rug pulls and the dollar losses involved. Good for learning what goes wrong and seeing actual loss figures.
- For educators who post real trade logs / P&L: look at CryptoCred (Twitter / Discord) or public portfolios on TradingView/eToro. Note: full, audited track records are rare; be skeptical and prefer independently verifiable sources.

If you meant specifically (B) — an educator or service that runs a live, independently verifiable account and publishes both gains and losses — tell me and I’ll search for currently active services with audited track records (those are uncommon and often tied to regulated funds).

Which of the two (general education vs. live P&L transparency) do you want? I’ll recommend the single best match.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
